theme_note: These passages issue or renew a collective call against the Patriots/28-3 canvas target; they vary from first alerts and broad enlistment to renewed calls, Void recruitment, and a last pre-close push.

second_order: working out how to change the score together
theme_note: These passages turn the wish to alter the target into instructions or coordinated pixel tactics; proposals vary between links, timers, digit edits, templates, target choice, coloured pushes, and a twenty-person blitz.

second_order: arguing whether the canvas fight is worth caring about
theme_note: These passages contest whether preserving, erasing, or even discussing the target matters; reasons vary between the saved final picture, humour, deserved humiliation, futility, and treating r/place as a distraction.

second_order: arguing whether five-minute placements can beat bots
theme_note: These passages work out whether manual persistence can overcome a larger crowd or reported bots, alts, scripts, and alliances; they range from failure reports and withdrawal to claims of manpower, continued trying, captcha hopes, and objections that warnings are defeatist.

second_order: recruiting, thanking, and bargaining with canvas allies
theme_note: These passages seek, acknowledge, or assess help from other subreddits and canvas groups; what varies is whether help is offered, thanked, requested, reported as erased, or exchanged for help elsewhere.

second_order: proposing something to make instead of only erasing
theme_note: These passages propose alternative visible work rather than bare deletion; designs vary among a Giants score, Georgia flag, deflated ball, Falcons logo, Manningface, and using existing artwork to cover the target.

second_order: trading rivalry and personal taunts in canvas threads
theme_note: These passages use the organising threads to trade 28-3, football, social-life, and conduct insults with visitors; turns vary between escalating, rebuking, mocking, demanding flair, offering private talk, and trying to exit.

second_order: mocking endless trade talk with an impossible trade
theme_note: The post and replies parody repetitive roster proposals by treating Ray Lewis, impossible draft compensation, and Poe as mock solutions to every need.

second_order: marking April Fools with foolish draft picks
theme_note: These passages conduct the room's own April Fools prompt by nominating and debating foolish Falcons draft choices, including a sarcastic Matt Ryan answer.

second_order: sharing and reacting to fake Falcons news
theme_note: These passages circulate and respond to fake Super Bowl stories and related April Fools articles; reactions range from collecting versions and laughing to rejecting them or resenting the reminder.

second_order: reversing football loyalties for April Fools
theme_note: These Daily Discussion turns deliberately reverse Saints loyalties, player judgments, and coaching preferences, while other replies identify or answer the joke in the room's ordinary rivalry language.

second_order: turning a fake trade into real roster debate
theme_note: These replies begin by believing or exposing a fake Sherman trade, then use it to debate cornerbacks, running backs, money, loyalty, and what would make a better joke.

second_order: keeping ordinary sports talk going in Daily Discussions
theme_note: These turns keep the catch-all threads doing their usual work alongside the jokes and canvas call: reporting Atlanta United and a player meeting, repeating Rise Up and Saints rivalry, welcoming baseball, and predicting the season.

second_order: reporting the erase call reached Slack
theme_note: This single passage reports that the opening erase post was sent into the speaker's Slack; no other code establishes the same off-platform circulation practice.

second_order: making outside help wait on the Pats meme
theme_note: These exchanges answer another group's request by putting the Falcons' existing target first; one bargains with the Eagles appeal and another refuses a Georgia-G recolouring until the Pats meme is addressed.

second_order: turning the Georgia-G request into Tech–UGA rivalry
theme_note: These replies redirect a canvas recolouring request into familiar college rivalry and cross-subreddit recognition; they vary between rejecting the rival, naming where the dispute travels, objecting to a nickname, and asking supporters to back both teams.

second_order: settling what the finished canvas means
theme_note: After placement ends, these passages argue over the surviving 28-3 score, whether Falcons made a logo, and whether the taunt will last; answers vary between celebration, counter-taunts, other scores, and predicting it will fade.
